harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook, run from node2 (the configured control_node, which has ansible-core installed) against node1, that serves a package repository from local storage on node1 and installs a package (cowsay) from it while the usual remote Ubuntu apt mirrors are unreachable. The playbook staged the .deb via apt-get download into /srv/local-repo, built a Packages index with apt-ftparchive, registered a trusted file:// apt source, made the remote mirrors unreachable by redirecting their hostnames to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts (a reversible disruption), ran apt-get update and captured its output showing connection-refused errors for archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com alongside successful reads from the local repo, installed cowsay purely from the local repo, verified it runs, then restored /etc/hosts and re-verified remote reachability. Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol for both node1 and node2: captured pre-restart boot IDs and service/data health, issued systemctl reboot via a backgrounded ack-then-disconnect pattern, polled until each node was reachable again, and proved changed boot IDs plus recovered SSH/Ansible connectivity, the intact local repo, and the still-installed/functional cowsay package on node1 after its reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (Ubuntu 24.04, apt-get/dpkg/apt-ftparchive present, no Ansible) and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, ansible-core 2.20.5, ansible.cfg with remote_user antrieb) to confirm node2 is the configured control_node.

Fixed node1's non-functional sshd (missing host keys) via ssh-keygen -A and enabled/started ssh.service; created the antrieb user with NOPASSWD sudo and authorized both the cluster keypair and node2's ansible id_rsa.pub so Ansible could reach node1.
Verified ansible -m ping connectivity from node2 to node1 using a new inventory.ini.

Manually rehearsed the local-repo-under-outage workflow on node1 end to end (download .deb, build repo index, register file:// source, block remote mirrors via /etc/hosts, apt-get update/install, verify with cowsay, then fully revert) before encoding it as Ansible.

Authored /root/repo-play/local-repo.yml on node2: purge-then-baseline the target package, refresh apt while remote is reachable, stage the .deb into /srv/local-repo, build/compress a Packages index, register a trusted local apt source, back up /etc/hosts, redirect Ubuntu mirror hostnames to 127.0.0.1, run apt-get update and assert the local repo was consulted while remote sources failed, install cowsay strictly from the local repo, verify functionality, then restore /etc/hosts and refresh apt again.

Ran --syntax-check then executed the playbook against node1 from node2; observed 20 ok/11 changed tasks with no failures, including explicit Err: Connection refused lines for archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com during the outage window and a working cowsay ASCII-art proof.

Independently re-verified on node1: cowsay installed and runnable, /srv/local-repo contents present, /etc/hosts diffed identical to its pre-disruption backup, and a live curl to archive.ubuntu.com returning HTTP 200 confirming remote reachability was restored.
Captured pre-restart boot IDs and health (ssh active, cowsay installed, local repo present on node1; ansible functional on node2) for both nodes.

Restarted node1 via a backgrounded systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnection; polled until reachable; confirmed a changed boot ID and that ssh, the installed cowsay package, the local repo files, and the apt source file all survived and the package still runs.
Restarted node2 the same way only after node1's recovery was confirmed; polled until reachable; confirmed a changed boot ID and that ansible-core still functions and can still reach/ping node1.

evidence.requirement: Local package repository served from local storage on node1
evidence.summary: cowsay .deb downloaded into /srv/local-repo and apt-ftparchive-generated Packages/Packages.gz index built from that local directory, then registered as a trusted file:// apt source.

evidence.requirement: Package installed from the local repo while usual remote repositories are unreachable (via Ansible)
evidence.summary: Full ansible-playbook run from control node node2 against node1: blocked archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com via /etc/hosts, ran apt-get update showing 'Connection refused' errors for the remote mirrors while the local file:// repo served Packages successfully, then apt install cowsay succeeded and /usr/games/cowsay produced output, all within the single playbook execution.

evidence.requirement: Disruption (blocked remote repos) was reversible and reverted
evidence.summary: Post-playbook check on node1: dpkg confirms cowsay installed, /srv/local-repo contents intact, diff of /etc/hosts against its pre-disruption backup shows no differences (fully restored), and a live curl to archive.ubuntu.com returns HTTP 200, confirming remote reachability was restored.

evidence.requirement: Implementation uses Ansible from the correct control node, not ad hoc shell
evidence.summary: Confirmed node2 is the node with ansible-core installed (the configured control_node), established working ansible ping connectivity to node1, and syntax-checked the playbook before running it for real.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 96c08b66... with ssh active and cowsay installed; issued backgrounded systemctl reboot that returned before disconnection; observed connection reset/timeout while down; polled back to reachable; confirmed new boot_id 9984bae7... plus ssh active, cowsay still installed and functional, and local repo files intact post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id a6937a34... with ansible-core functional and playbook file present; issued backgrounded systemctl reboot that returned before disconnection; observed connection reset/timeout while down; polled back to reachable; confirmed new boot_id 09a93698..., ansible-core still functional, and ansible ping to node1 still succeeding post-reboot of both nodes.
